anchorFacts: The Outfield squeeze for next season. 5 Outfielders for 3 positions.

Danny Horn is your starting CF. A returing MVP and the best player in baseball makes it an easy decision. Darrin Davis figures to be your DH as he remains under contract and showed his numbers did not decline, albiet he was injured. Davis has missed substantial time twice over the past three seasons. Vladimir is entering his peak and put up his best numbers of his career last season. Rates as a clutch perfomer and is essentially who you chose over Peter Busch last offseason.

If those spots are set then you have three players for one left field opening. Desmond Morton is you highest rated prospect with 5 tools and has shown success at the MLB level, Frank Reyna is a power hitter with a mass of potential that also showed success. JR Rosado performed well in his major league experience and had good contact numbers but may trend as a role player in the grand scheme. What is the choice Paulson should make here.

sources.name: Desmond Morton
sources.quote: Honestly, the coaches haven't given me a clear answer yet. They know I've shown I can play at this level, but with Danny locked in center and Vladimir coming off the year he had, it's a real squeeze for left. I'm just trying to control what I can—show up, work, and let my play make the case. I know Frank and J.R. are pushing too, so it's not something I lose sleep over. The team's got a good problem, and whoever gets the spot, we're all pulling the same direction.

sources.name: Frank Reyna
sources.quote: Honestly, I don't think about separating myself from Desmond or JR. I think about what I bring that they don't. They've both proven they belong, no question. But I'm a power bat, and in this ballpark, that plays. I've shown I can do it at this level. The way I see it, the decision isn't about who's better — it's about what the lineup needs. And I'm going to make sure that answer is me.

sources.name: Vladimir Gonzalez
sources.quote: Honestly, the vibe is a lot less tense than you'd think. We all know the business side of it — somebody's gonna get moved or sent down, that's just how it goes. What I tell the young guys is you can't control what Paulson decides. You just control how you show up. And truth be told, it's a good problem for the A's to have. Means we got depth, and that's how you win. I earned my spot, sure, but I remember what it was like trying to crack a crowded room. You just hope the decision gets made quick so whoever it is lands somewhere they can play.

excludedLeads.text: The clubhouse whiteboard had Morton's name written in the left field slot before being erased — could be nothing, could be a hint at the front office's lean.
A coach was overheard saying the decision might come down to who fits the lineup's defensive needs, not just the bat.
